chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: The Rhythm Club and the Big Apple
summary: The Rhythm Club was the musicians' hiring hall where Moore got jobs; pay varied by band size; the Big Apple was just a hangout.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, during this time that you came to New York and you were in New York... You got into New York around 1928. What about the Rhythm Club? Who were some of the...? Did you go there often? I understand that the musicians used to hang out at the Rhythm Club.
Yeah, we used to...
[END OF TAPE 2, SIDE B]
We're talking about the Rhythm Club.
[PAUSE]
...headquarters. We'd hang out there. That's where we got all the jobs. That's where I got my job, I was
Moore (II) - 38
there, when I worked with Eubie Blake.
I see. How would the jobs come about at the Rhythm Club? Would musicians who were looking for other musicians come in? Or were there notices posted on the wall?

Well, we went there to meet different musicians. They had a pool table there; we played pool to pass away the time... The Rhythm Club was known all over during that time. If people here in the city wanted to give dances or something, they'd call up the Rhythm Club for the musicians. Anything over three pieces, they had to appoint somebody for the leader. The dealer, he'd tell me that I'm the leader. He'd say, 'Freddie Moore, get me three pieces.' I'd get three pieces. I'm supposed to get a little bit more on the job, sometimes paying eight dollars, sometimes twelve dollars -- but the leader gets fifteen. It's according to the amount of pieces. Sometimes there are three pieces, five pieces, eight pieces, a ten-piece band. Played for dances, cocktails, weddings...
I see. Now, this Rhythm Club was upstairs? Or was it on...?
On the level.
It was on the level.
Moore (II) - 39
Right the way it is now, 133rd Street and Lenox...
So it was always at that place. Okay. What about this gin-mill at 135th Street called the Big Apple?
Yea...
Was that there when you came to New York?
Yeah, right there. On the corner.
What took place there?
It was a very small place. But they never had no music there. They tried it with piano and drums there, but the place was too small. It had a big name, but the place didn't stay full.
It was more of a hangout than anything else.
Yes.
